pr.title: Add the trip.here website, and serve the installer from https://trip.here/install.sh
pr.head: a8b88de5afcff6d0fcb91e18524b67bf3a80dc3c

summary: trip is a small daemon that keeps terminal sessions alive after you close a window. Until now, the only place to learn about it was the GitHub README, and the install command was a long raw.githubusercontent.com URL. This pull request gives trip a home page at https://trip.here and shortens the install command to curl -fsSL https://trip.here/install.sh | bash.

The site is one static HTML page in a new site/ directory, with no build step. Vercel, a static hosting service, deploys it from a project whose root directory is site. A Vercel configuration file, site/vercel.json, decides what /install.sh returns. It does not hold a copy of the installer. It tells Vercel to fetch the installer from GitHub at the v0 tag and return it under the trip.here URL.

v0 is the tag the release workflow moves to each new release, last, after the release exists. So trip.here always serves the newest release's installer, and a release needs no site redeploy. trip upgrade, the command that moves an existing install to the newest release, still downloads the installer for one exact tag straight from GitHub, and this change leaves it alone.

The README and the installer's usage comment now show the trip.here command. The change does not point trip.here's DNS at Vercel; that happens outside the repository. Until it does, the new command does not work.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Rewrite: Vercel fetches another URL and returns its response under the site's own URL. The client sees no redirect.
  • v0: the git tag that always names the newest 0.x release. The installer builds the source at v0 by default.
  • ignoreCommand: a shell command Vercel runs before a build. Exit status 0 skips the deployment.
  • Projector site: the separate GitHub Pages site at ninjudd.com/trip, built from the README, docs/, and review summaries.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One open finding: the page's transcript shows a session chooser that trip enter does not draw when run from the home directory.
  • Merge only after trip.here serves the installer. Today trip.here is a registrar URL forward with nothing listening on HTTPS.
  • The rewrite, the tag it reads, and the caching headers were checked and match the release process.

groups.title: Serving the installer from trip.here
groups.kicker: What https://trip.here/install.sh returns, and where the new URL is published
intro: Users pipe the installer straight into bash, so what /install.sh returns matters more than anything else on the site. site/vercel.json rewrites that one path to https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ninjudd/trip/v0/install.sh. Because it is a rewrite, the response comes back with a 200 under the trip.here URL, and curl -fsSL needs no redirect support. Both hops use HTTPS.

Serving from the v0 tag rather than from main keeps the installer and the source it builds on the same release. The installer's TRIP_REF setting defaults to v0 too, so a script fetched from trip.here builds the release it came from.

The README's install section and the usage comment at the top of install.sh switch to the trip.here command. The README also drops a sentence saying the command works only after the first release, which stopped being true at 0.1.0.

checks.text: No other file names an installer URL that should change. src/client/upgrade.rs builds raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/<tag>/install.sh for the tag it checks against, the e2e tests point that at local copies through TRIP_RAW_URL, and .github/scripts/release.py names no installer URL. Checked by searching the head for every installer URL.

trip.here does not yet serve the installer. Nothing answers on port 443, and plain HTTP answers with a registrar's redirect. Merging before DNS moves publishes a README install command that fails with only curl's connection error.

files.note: The Vercel configuration: the installer rewrite, clean URLs, and a check that skips deploys for commits that leave site/ alone.

checks.text: GitHub serves the rewrite's destination with content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8 and cache-control: max-age=300, so trip.here can lag a release by about five minutes at most. Checked with a read-only request to the raw URL.

git diff --quiet HEAD^ HEAD -- . compares only the newest commit with its parent. A push of several commits whose last one leaves site/ alone skips the deploy. Every commit to main is a squash merge, so production deploys are not affected.

files.note: Only the usage comment changes, to show the trip.here command. The script's behavior is unchanged.
The install command now uses trip.here, and an outdated sentence about the first release is gone.

groups.title: The home page
groups.kicker: One static page that says what trip is and how to install it
intro: site/index.html is a single page with inline CSS and one small inline script for the copy button. It loads no third-party script, font, or tracker. It has an install command with a copy button, a terminal transcript of a session that survives a closed window, a list of what trip does, and the terminal setup for macOS Terminal and iTerm2. For everything else it links to the README.
The page adapts to light and dark mode, and stops the blinking cursor when the reader asks for reduced motion. Its muted text keeps a contrast ratio of at least 5.4:1 in both schemes.

checks.text: The page's claims about Ctrl-\, trip screen, trip log, trip send, trip on, trip wrap, trip upgrade, and the terminal setup match the README and the code. Checked by reading each against the README and src/client.

files.note: The whole site: the hero and install command, the transcript, the feature list, and the terminal setup.

checks.text: Open finding: this trip enter runs in the home directory, where row 0 would be a new session for the home workspace and would start selected. The transcript instead shows row 0 as acme/webapp.1 with acme/webapp selected, and the header of the in-session chooser (esc back) rather than the q cancels header that trip enter prints.
When the clipboard API is missing or refuses the write, the copy button does nothing and shows no message.

files.note: A small prompt-and-cursor icon in the page's colors.

groups.title: Ignoring Vercel's local files
groups.kicker: Keeping the Vercel CLI's project link and tokens out of git
intro: vercel link writes a .vercel directory and can write .env files that hold a token. Both patterns have no leading slash, so they match at any depth, including inside site/. No file already tracked in the repository matches either one.

checks.text: The existing Projector site on GitHub Pages builds from the README, docs/, and review summaries, and never reads site/, so the two sites do not collide.
